VideoMonitor is a Windows desktop app for miners (yt-dlp downloads) and runners (FFmpeg encodes): folders or URL lists, presets, schedules, optional miner→runner linking, tray, and notifications.
About is a main tab (not inside the page scroller). Left keyboard shortcut hints. A with F2 opens this tab. F1 is the full shortcut overlay (Esc closes it).
Short map of the objects you edit in the UI. Screens and Settings pages spell out the controls.
What you need

Letterbox is an FFmpeg preset path on a runner: pad a horizontal frame into a vertical one (or the reverse) instead of stretching. It lives on the Runners row and in the preset wizard, not as its own Settings group.
A miner is one yt-dlp job: a source (URL, directory, playlist file, or web shortcut) and a destination folder. Drill is the main action — it builds a download queue, then downloads items.
The Performance tab shows live system and per-runner/miner metrics while work is active (and optionally in the background on other tabs).

Press F1 in the app for the full overlay. Esc closes it. This page mirrors the product reference (English).

Place VideoMonitor.toml beside the executable (or let the app create defaults when you add a runner/miner). Start the program. Open Settings → Miners (yt-dlp) and run Verify yt-dlp setup if downloads are planned. Open Runners, select row A, set Path to originals, Mask, FFmpeg options, and Output (sub)dir, then press Start (or G with F2 shortcuts on). For a quick test, point at a small folder with one or two short MP4 files and a conservative CRF preset. The status column moves through states such as MONITORING, RUNNING, IDLE, Queued, Paused. The Performance tab shows CPU and per-runner speed when monitoring is enabled.

[app] log_level = "info" [[runners]] name = "Archive" path = "D:\\Videos\\Incoming" mask = "*.mp4" ffmpeg_args = "-c:v libx264 -crf 23 -c:a aac -b:a 192k" output_subdir = "encoded" overwrite_original = false [[miners]] name = "Channel" source_path_or_url = "https://www.youtube.com/@example" destination_dir = "D:\\Downloads\\Channel" ytdlp_args = "" Adjust paths for your machine. UI edits write back to the same structure.

Letterbox is an FFmpeg preset path on a runner: pad a horizontal frame into a vertical one (or the reverse) instead of stretching. It lives on the Runners row and in the preset wizard, not as its own Settings group. Runners row — Letterbox control and generated FFmpeg options. Typical flow: Select a runner. Turn Letterbox on (or open the preset wizard and pick horizontal→vertical or vertical→horizontal). The app writes FFmpeg filter args (pad / related) into that runner’s options. Optionally save the slot so other runners can load the same pad. Preset labels that come from the wizard include “letterbox” so the bank stays recognizable. Allow runner FFmpeg preset chain (Coordination) still applies if you chain slots with Ctrl+Shift+click. Encode start, CPU cap, and folder watch are unchanged: Runners, CPU.

Runners and Miners share the same preset bank model. FFmpeg options (Runners) and yt-dlp options (Miners) live in two places: Layer Where it lives When it changes Row draft runner.ffmpeg_args / miner.ytdlp_args Immediately as you type in the options field Preset bank [app] → ffmpeg_presets / yt_dlp_presets (+ labels) Only on explicit save paths (see below) Typing in the field does not update the global preset bank by default. That prevents accidental overwrites when you click another preset slot. Runners preset bank — click loads, Ctrl+click writes. Miners preset bank — same click / Ctrl+click model.

Open Settings → Coordination (near Process files on FFmpeg change and Allow runner FFmpeg preset chain): Option Config key Default Auto save runner preset on edit auto_save_runner_preset_on_edit off Auto save miner preset on edit auto_save_miner_preset_on_edit off Each tab is independent. The legacy option Save preset names on mouse click only was removed from the UI and is forced to false in config sanitization.

flowchart TD edit[Edit in options field] --> rowOnly[Update runner/miner row only] rowOnly --> autoOn{Auto-save ON for this tab?} autoOn -->|No| noBank[Preset bank unchanged] autoOn -->|Yes| debounce[Wait ~600 ms after last keystroke] debounce --> grammar{Grammar OK and non-empty?} grammar -->|No| noCommit[No bank write] grammar -->|Yes| same{Draft equals active slot S?} same -->|Yes| noCommit same -->|No| commit[Write to active slot S in app bank] commit --> ui[Green border + success banner + save config]
Only the current runner/miner row changes. Other preset slots in [app] stay as they were. Switching slots loads the bank text into the editor without writing your draft into the clicked slot.

After you stop typing for about 600 ms, the app may commit only if: A preset slot is already selected (active slot S). FFmpeg / yt-dlp grammar checks pass. The draft is non-empty and differs from what is stored in slot S (normalized comparison). The draft is not already stored in a different slot (duplicate options are not auto-written). On success: Slot S in the bank is updated (label is re-suggested when needed). The options editor gets a green border for a few seconds. A success banner appears: Selected preset has been updated. Config is saved (debounced). Important: auto-save always writes to the slot that was selected before you edited (active_preset_slot / miner_active_preset_slot), never to a slot you only clicked afterward.

Click What happens Plain click slot B Load B into the editor (row draft). Does not write the bank. Ctrl+click slot N Modal: Write these options into slot N? Yes writes the current editor text into N. Ctrl+Shift+click (Runners) Adds/cycles the FFmpeg preset chain (up to 3), when chaining is enabled in Settings. Clicking B never silently overwrites B. Writing a slot is always Ctrl+click plus confirm.

Action Behavior Add (+) slot Opens wizard if empty/duplicate; otherwise creates a new bank slot with unique options Double-click slot Opens preset wizard for that slot Drag preset chips Reorders slots in the bank Preset wizard → Create Explicit save into the chosen slot Apply preset (bulk load) still loads into the editor without rewriting the bank.

A runner is one FFmpeg pipeline: input tree (or explicit file list), file mask, FFmpeg arguments, and output location. Up to eight rows can be visible in the strip; more slots exist in config but hidden rows live in the “pocket” until shown (9 / row visibility shortcuts). Runners tab — table, selected row, Start / presets. Selected runner — path, mask, FFmpeg options, output.

Block Purpose Control Start / Pause / Stop / Resume; Queued(N) when waiting in sequential mode. Path to originals Root folder for scan mode. Changing to a different directory root clears the manual Selected files list. Mask Glob filter (*.mp4, etc.). FFmpeg Argument string; preset chips below; optional preset chain (up to 3) when enabled in Settings. Output (sub)dir Relative or absolute output tree; VM@ metadata tags on outputs. Selected files Manual queue table (optional). Progress / status Current file bar, ETC line (click to cycle display mode), file stats. Red directory does not exist banner debounces for 1 s while typing; use Browse for immediate validation.

Mode How work is discovered Scan Walk Path + Mask; optional monitor for new files. Manual Only paths in Selected files; order = processing order. Add files… requires the same folder as existing queue entries. Select files… replaces the queue. Multi-select: Ctrl+click toggle, Shift+click range. Remove on active row removes all selected; Shift+R removes without confirm (if confirm enabled). Delete / Backspace follow confirm rules.

Hidden by default. On Runners tab, hold Ctrl+Space to show per-row Playlist buttons. Collects sources from manual list order or directory full_list order. Writes playlist per Settings format (M3U/M3U8, filename pattern with optional duration). Queued exports: multiple clicks enqueue; one background job at a time; strip shows progress and “N more in queue”. Cancel stops the active export only.

Outputs can carry VM@ comment tags (PARAMS, skip). Manual table: Faded name + @ when tagged processed. Right-click: tag skip, clear tags, remove. Orange tint when PARAMS mismatch vs current FFmpeg and overwrite rules apply. Output extension (optional) — per-runner target extension; stem may become name_srcext.mp4 when recontainerizing.
Sequential — one runner at a time globally (others show Queued). Parallel — multiple runners can encode together subject to CPU limits.

Outside configured hours, runner may show Scheduled (orange) instead of starting new work. Starting label appears when started but not yet busy inside an allowed window. Edit the window in App behavior → Deferred actions. Work schedule editor (App behavior → Deferred actions → Edit…). Outside these hours a runner may show Scheduled.

Miners can link to a runner letter. When coordination allows, miner completion triggers the linked runner. See Settings → Coordination.
When experimental cleanup is enabled globally (App behavior → Disk space cleanup), each runner can opt in and mark Originals or Outputs as sacrifice candidates (hazard border stripes).

VideoMonitor can keep running from the Windows notification area: close or hide the window without exiting the process. Tooltip content is chosen in Settings. Tray icon context menu (Show / Hide / Pause / Exit). Notification-area icon (color or monochrome from Appearance). Piece Where Icon style (color / monochrome) Appearance Tooltip: app name / counts / primary job + ETA App behavior → Tray & status bar Close or hide to tray same Settings group Accent on the icon Appearance accent Left-click the icon typically shows or focuses the window; right-click opens the menu. Q (F2 layer) exits without confirmation — that does quit the process, it does not hide to tray. If Settings or About look stale after an update, check that an old instance is not still in the tray.
Practical workflows. Adjust paths, letters, and options to your setup. Typical layout — Runners tab, three rows, selected runner C with FFmpeg options.

Goal: Everything matching *.mp4 under D:\Inbox becomes H.264 in D:\Inbox\VM@720p, including files that arrive overnight. Runner A — Path D:\Inbox, mask *.mp4, FFmpeg -c:v libx264 -crf 23, output subdir VM@720p. Settings → Coordination — enable Monitor unprocessed files (or press M on Runners with F2 shortcuts on). Start runner A. Leave Sequential or Parallel per taste (F2: S / P). Minimize to tray. New files are picked up on the next scan cycle. Tip: Enable Process files on FFmpeg change only if you intentionally want re-encode when you edit options; otherwise changing CRF mid-run can mark existing outputs for overwrite (see Runners file stats line).

Goal: No folder scan — only chosen files, in a fixed order. Runner B — set path to the folder that contains the files (mask still applies to adds). Select files… (or Ctrl+Shift+Enter) and pick the five files. Reorder in the Selected files table: drag rows, or Ctrl+↑/↓ to move selection (contiguous block moves one step; non-contiguous selection compacts first). Start. The worker processes the list top to bottom; watcher mode does not refill from disk until you clear or change the list. Tip: Ctrl+Shift+Space focuses the manual queue when it is non-empty. Right-click a row for Tag as processed (VM@: skip) to skip files without deleting them.
documents.s: Scenario 2: Encode exactly five clips (manual queue)

documents.t: Goal: Build M3U/M3U8 from runner sources for VLC, car unit, etc. Configure runner sources (directory scan or manual list). On Runners tab, hold Ctrl+Space — each row shows Playlist instead of Start. Click Playlist on one or more runners. Exports run in a background queue (FIFO): while one playlist is built, you can queue more; progress strip shows active job and “N more in queue”. Release Ctrl+Space to hide the buttons again. Playlist path/format come from Settings → Coordination (playlist format, M3U8 filename pattern) and per-runner output layout. No FFmpeg encode runs for this action.
documents.s: Scenario 3: Export playlists for a player (no transcode)

documents.t: Goal: yt-dlp pulls into D:\DL\Channel; runner encodes to D:\Out. Miner C — Src URL https://www.youtube.com/@…, Destination D:\DL\Channel, set yt-dlp options (format, subs) via presets. Drill — queue fills (verify → scan → download). Review Download queue chips; click shared format tokens to paste into yt-dlp field. Runner D — Path D:\DL\Channel, mask *.mp4, destination elsewhere. Settings → Coordination — link miner C to runner D; optionally auto-start linked runner when miner batch completes. Start miner, then runner (or rely on auto-start). Tip: When a URL title is first resolved, the sanitized folder name may copy to the clipboard and flash in the status bar — useful when naming the destination folder.
documents.s: Scenario 4: Download a YouTube channel, then encode

documents.t: Goal: A directory of browser link files, not a single channel URL. Miner — Src path = folder containing .url / .webloc / .desktop shortcuts (or drop one shortcut onto the miner row with drag-and-drop enabled). Drill — listing walks the tree (respecting skip dirs like .git, node_modules). Or drop a .m3u / .m3u8 onto the miner row for playlist expansion.

Goal: Do not saturate the machine during work hours. Settings → CPU — set CPU limit (e.g. 40%). Enable Adaptive load to nudge effective cap within min/max while jobs run. Optional Start when lower — new encodes wait until system CPU stays below the limit for 5 seconds. Settings → App behavior → Work schedule — restrict runner activity to evening windows (orange Scheduled under tab when outside window).

Goal: When free space drops, delete oldest/largest sacrificial files from agreed trees. Settings → App behavior → Disk space cleanup — enable, set threshold and deletion preferences. On each runner row, enable Disk participation and choose Originals vs Outputs sacrifice. Hazard stripes on the row border indicate what may be deleted (orange originals, green outputs). Use only when you understand which trees are shared and backed up.
documents.s: Scenario 7: Low disk space on the encode volume

documents.t: Goal: Source or destination on \\server\share\… without treating brief disconnects as hard failures. Path vitality — enable in VideoMonitor.toml (path_vitality_*), prefer remote-only, tune probe interval and confirm failures. While Suspect, encode/download pauses without counting as permanent failure; Down triggers failure notifications.

Goal: Message on completion, Morse beep optional. Settings → Notifications — Telegram token/chat, templates with placeholders (%runner%, %files_count%, …). Per runner/miner Notify column — enable channels; all-off with sound-only still uses green styling for “sound only”. Edit sound for Morse templates (success vs failure differ). Store tokens in VideoMonitor.local.toml on shared configs.
documents.s: Scenario 9: Telegram when a batch finishes

documents.t: Goal: More space for Runners/Miners daily; charts only sometimes. Open Performance, uncheck Show Performance tab (pin on tab) or Ctrl+W while on Performance. Ctrl+Shift+T restores the tab in the strip without switching to it — stay on Runners and open Performance when ready.
documents.s: Scenario 10: Hide Performance tab until needed

Public GitHub for VideoMonitor help is vladimirzubkov/VideoMonitorDocs. Use Issues there to report bugs and suggest features. Do not paste passwords, API tokens, or full config files with secrets. In the app, About → Bugs and ideas opens the same GitHub chooser.
Open a bug report Include the app version (logo badge), OS, steps, and what you expected versus what happened.
Open a feature request Describe the problem or use case first; a proposed solution is optional.
Choose bug or idea
Beside the executable: VideoMonitor.toml (main) and optional VideoMonitor.local.toml (notification secrets). The UI saves on change. See Getting started.
Runners transcode with FFmpeg from folders or a manual file list. Miners download with yt-dlp from URLs, folders, or playlist files. They can be linked so a finished download starts an encode.
documents.s: Runners vs Miners — which do I use?

documents.t: Common causes: Runner Paused or outside work schedule (Scheduled on tab). Sequential mode while another runner holds the queue (Queued(N)). Start when lower waiting for CPU to drop (Settings → CPU). Empty path, bad mask, or manual queue empty. Path vitality Suspect / Down on network paths.
documents.s: Why does encode not start immediately?

documents.t: Run Verify yt-dlp setup in Settings; install Deno if prompted. On Windows, non-ASCII titles need UTF-8 pipe handling (built in; update yt-dlp if ancient). Check User-Agent and rate limits in Settings → Miners (yt-dlp).
documents.s: Why does yt-dlp fail or show wrong titles?

documents.t: Plain click loads a slot. Ctrl+click writes the current options into that slot after confirm. Ctrl+Shift+click on Runners builds a preset chain. Typing edits the row; with auto-save on, the active slot updates after a short pause. See Presets.
It should not — exports run on a background thread with a FIFO queue. Hold Ctrl+Space on Runners to show Playlist buttons; queue multiple runners one after another.
F1 in the app, About tab cheat sheet, or Shortcuts.

About → Bugs and ideas, or the Bugs and ideas page. Reports go to public GitHub Issues on VideoMonitorDocs (not email).

documents.t: Set GitHub owner/repo in config; About → Update program or startup policy under Settings → App behavior → Updates.

Confirm VideoMonitor.toml is valid TOML (no stray tabs; use the example under dev/config_examples/). Check log file path from Settings → App behavior log level; run from terminal once to see stderr. On Linux, display server / tray requirements for your desktop environment.

Verify ffmpeg and ffprobe on PATH (ffmpeg -version). Test the same FFmpeg string manually on one failing input. Container/codec hints (orange banner) — extension vs codec mismatch (e.g. VP9 into MP4). Output extension — stem_srcext.mp4 naming when retargeting extension.

Scheduled — outside work schedule window; wait or edit schedule (T with F2). Starting stuck — often cleared on re-Go; verify-all-done paths reset state; check path exists. Queued — sequential mode; another runner is active.
documents.s: Runner stuck on Starting or Scheduled

documents.t: Use Ctrl+↑/↓ after sort: first move materializes visual order into storage. Cursor keys follow display order (see Runners).
documents.s: Manual queue wrong order after sort

documents.t: Set Destination before download phase. URL vs folder: one shortcut per drop; no mixed folder+URL drop. Verify yt-dlp setup; update yt-dlp; install Deno for some sites.
documents.s: Miner queue empty or Drill does nothing

documents.t: Adaptive load changes effective cap, not always the slider line. Multiple parallel runners multiply load. Limit logical cores applies on new spawns; asterisk on Performance means old job used prior cap.
Turn off Monitor stats live on background (Settings → CPU → Performance charts).
Enable Path vitality for remote roots; Suspect pauses without permanent fail until Down confirmed.
Normal quit clears tray; Task Manager kill may leave a ghost icon until Explorer refresh. Use in-app exit when possible.
Test from Settings; check token/chat or SMTP port (465/587). Secrets in local.toml not overwritten by old main file copies. Notify column off for row = no Telegram/mail (sound-only still possible).
Check .video-monitor-replace.log next to exe. Antivirus may lock exe — retry; backup ZIP optional in Settings. Private GitHub releases need token in config.
Note runner/miner letter, status text, and last log lines. Compare with Recipes and Settings.
VideoMonitor beta is free for non-commercial use. Optional donations support development via Stripe Checkout.

Donations are voluntary and do not unlock commercial use. After a donation, in-app reminders may pause for a period depending on amount (see app FAQ). Payment data is processed by Stripe; we do not operate a separate license database.
Sign-in links your Stripe customer record (donation quiet period, future license) to an account via Clerk (GitHub, Google, or email). Session tokens are stored encrypted on your device.
Commercial licenses (personal and organization) are tested in beta but not sold until announced. The app hides purchase buttons until enabled remotely.
Please use About → Bugs and ideas in the app (GitHub Issues on the public docs repo). Do not send product feedback by email.
We may end the beta remotely (policy URL). You will be prompted to update; commercial terms will apply when sales open.
VideoMonitor is distributed as a desktop application. This page describes data flows for the beta program (donations, optional sign-in, public GitHub Issues).

Encoding configuration (VideoMonitor.toml, presets, paths). Optional log file when Save log to file is enabled. Encrypted session token after sign-in (platform keychain / DPAPI / machine-bound encryption). Last crash summary (VideoMonitor.last-crash.json) if the program panicked — removed when you dismiss or send a report.

Service Purpose Data Stripe Donations (and later commercial licenses) Email from Checkout, payment metadata, quiet-period timestamps in Customer metadata Clerk Optional sign-in (GitHub, Google, email) Account identifiers; we do not store your password GitHub Public bug reports and feature requests Whatever you submit in Issues (public repo VideoMonitorDocs)
The app may call our license API (license_api_base_url in config) to read beta flags (donations on/off, minimum version). No runner paths or media filenames are sent in that request.
You may request access or deletion of personal data held in Stripe or Clerk through their dashboards or support. For Issues on GitHub, use GitHub’s tools or contact us via a new issue.
Use Bugs and ideas in the app (About tab) or open an issue in the documentation repository.

Top-left Settings group. Controls how often miners are polled, how runners share the CPU queue, and how a finished miner can start a runner. Settings → Coordination and Monitoring. Option Typical default Meaning Enable monitoring on Background watch of miner sources / runner folders Sequential vs Parallel Sequential One runner encode at a time vs overlapping encodes Monitor unprocessed files on Runner watches the source folder for new work Process files on FFmpeg change on Re-queue when the runner's FFmpeg options change Miner poll interval ~5 s How often miners refresh listings / titles Minimum age seconds Ignore files newer than this (still being written) Unwrap archives off Expand archives in miner sources when supported Volume / session hints — Default ETC / TL / volume line on Miners Allow runner FFmpeg preset chain off Enable Ctrl+Shift+click preset chains Auto save runner preset on edit off Debounced write of the active runner slot while typing Auto save miner preset on edit off Same for miners Min savings to encode — Skip encode if estimated savings are below the threshold Create playlist — Playlist export from Runners (also Ctrl+Space on the tab) Show linking menu in miners Where the miner→runner letter menu appears Allow hidden miners/runners to work off Hidden rows still run Clear / apply VM tags — Tag processed originals in the runner path Linking: set a miner’s link letter to a runner. When coordination allows, miner completion starts that runner. Details: Miners, Runners. Work schedule (when jobs may start) is edited under App behavior → Deferred actions, not in this group.

Top-right Settings group (CPU load), above Miners (yt-dlp). Caps encoding load, optional adaptive tuning, sequential/parallel launch, and Performance-tab sampling. Settings → CPU load (cap, adaptive, launch, Performance charts). Option Typical default Meaning CPU limit ~80% Target cap on encoding CPU (10–100%). Drawn on the Performance chart. Start when lower and adaptive load use this as the baseline. Use floor for threads calculation — Floor when mapping the cap onto FFmpeg thread counts Limit logical cores — Restrict how many logical cores encodes may use Adaptive load off While jobs run, sample system CPU (~5 s) and nudge the effective FFmpeg cap inside Min / Max. Does not rewrite the CPU limit slider or TOML. Start when lower still uses the slider. Adaptive Min / Max 10–100% Bounds for that effective cap Launch runners Sequential / Parallel Sequential Queue policy (also S / P with F2 on Runners) Start when lower per runner Job waits until CPU stays under the cap for ~5 seconds Sample interval ms How often Performance charts sample History window sec How much chart history to keep Monitor stats live on background — Keep sampling on other tabs (slower). Off if the UI stutters while encoding. Update when the source is updatable. yt-dlp: version (source) Same for yt-dlp. not found / detecting… PATH / sidecar missing, or still probing Verify yt-dlp setup and Install Deno live under Miners (yt-dlp), not here. Same Settings column as CPU load, section Miners (yt-dlp). Network identity, throttling, subtitle defaults, and tool readiness. Settings → Miners (yt-dlp): cookies, delay, subtitles, Verify.

Option Config key Typical default Meaning Cookies file miners_cookies_file empty Netscape cookies.txt for yt-dlp. Browse picks the file. Browser hint miners_browser none If there is no cookies file, yt-dlp can take cookies from Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Opera / Safari (--cookies-from-browser). User-Agent miners_user_agent empty Override the HTTP User-Agent. Delay (sec) from / to miners_delay_min_sec / miners_delay_max_sec 5–30 Random pause between requests. Limit rate miners_limit_rate empty yt-dlp -r style cap, e.g. 1M. Export cookies with a browser extension (for example “Get cookies.txt locally”) if you prefer a file over Browser hint.

Network / UNC paths can go Suspect then Down. Runners (and miners that use those paths) pause instead of spinning on I/O errors. Health shows on the row; keys live in [app] in VideoMonitor.toml. Runner/miner row showing path vitality (Suspect / Down).
